d.a: Occurrence: Clevelandella philipi was found in the hindgut of two Panesthiinae species from Papua New Guinea: ASS and STH from the same locality (Wanang 3). Of STH individuals, all of which were juveniles, 30 % harboured C. philipi. Since only two adults of the STH population (both males) were dissected, no conclusions can be reached about possible life-stage specificity. In the ASS population, C. philipi was present in 37 % of cockroach individuals regardless of age and sex. When present, the ciliate is typically abundant. In ASS the infection with C. philipi sp. nov. frequently (90 %) co-occurred with C. ananiasi sp. nov., requiring care in identification.
